title: fix(objectql,metadata-protocol): refuse aggregate queries that answered a wrong table, and an empty aggregate list
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XW13v6b99WMmzHuTFCwjmae)_

Fixes #25818
Fixes #25819
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: 6399831537

The aggregate door answered three malformed queries with a plausible wrong table under 200, and an empty `aggregations` list with `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` for a registered object. All four now answer 400, naming the position. The claim is `6407789444`; the seat claim on #25819, `6408744205`, names the same branch. Branch `claude/project-thread-6vh3z0` is the card thread's harness-pinned branch: one commit, `46a0a7df`, on `main` `cb0a2fcf4f`.

## What changes

**#25818, at the engine's `aggregate` entry** (`packages/objectql/src/aggregate-query-shape-door.ts`, called from `engine.ts` right after the structured-JSON group door and the aggregate × field-type door):

| query | before (`main` `cb0a2fcf4f`, through `findData`) | now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `groupBy: [{ field: 'name', dateGranularity: 'month' }]` on a `text` field | `200 [{ name: null, n: 3 }]` | `400 INVALID_FIELD`, `path: groupBy.0.dateGranularity` |
| the same on a `number` field | `200 [{ amount: '1970-01', n: 3 }]` | `400 INVALID_FIELD` |
| the same on a `time` field | `200 [{ at_time: null, n: 3 }]` | `400 INVALID_FIELD` |
| `aggregations: [{ count, alias: 'n' }, { sum amount, alias: 'n' }]` | `200 [{ n: 60 }]` | `400 INVALID_QUERY`, `path: aggregations.1.alias` |
| `groupBy: ['status'], aggregations: [{ count, alias: 'status' }]` | `200 [{ status: 2 }, { status: 1 }]` | `400 INVALID_QUERY`, `path: aggregations.0.alias` |
| two group entries projecting one column (`opened_on` by month and by year) | `200 [{ opened_on: '2026', n: 1 }, { opened_on: '2026', n: 2 }]` | `400 INVALID_QUERY`, `path: groupBy.1.field` |

- **"A date field" is the declared type's class**, read by `declaredFieldClasses` (`having-filter.ts`), which is the reading `in-memory-aggregation.ts`'s `calendarDayGroupFields` buckets a `date` field by. A `date` (`CALENDAR_DATE_TYPES`) and a `datetime` (`INSTANT_TYPES`) pass. A field the declaration cannot type is not judged: undeclared (the ingress door answers an unknown one first; a system column the map does not declare buckets as before), a `formula`, or a registry-less host. `driver-sql`'s pushdown reads its own column registry (`temporalFieldKind`), so the engine door judges before either face.
- **A column name** is a group entry's name, or `alias ?? field` for the object form (the name `applyInMemoryAggregation` and `driver-sql` project), and an aggregation's `alias`. An alias moves the group column, so `groupBy: [{ field: 'status', alias: 's' }]` with an aggregation aliased `status` is served.
- **Every door agrees** because the check sits in `engine.aggregate`: the REST query route and its dispatcher twin (both through `findData`), the analytics ObjectQL strategy, the MCP data bridge, a flow or a hook. The engine's `INVALID_FIELD` / `INVALID_QUERY` with `status: 400` reaches the wire through `mapDataError` unchanged (pinned below).
- The two group entries projecting one column is the same defect class as the alias collision (one row column, two values) and closes in the same walk, so it rides here as a bounded in-place fix (same class, mechanical, same files, same gate family). Its base answer is the last row of the table above.

**#25819, at `findData`** (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, after `assertAggregationFieldsExist`): an aggregate axis sent as an empty list, with no non-empty axis beside it, answers `400 INVALID_QUERY`, naming `'query.aggregations'` (or `'query.groupBy'`, or both) as empty. `{ groupBy: ['status'], aggregations: [] }` and `{ groupBy: [], aggregations: [count] }` are served as before.

- **Where the 404 came from** (measured, the card had not traced it): the routing read `[]` as "no aggregate" and handed the key to `engine.find`, whose unknown-option refusal (`engine.ts:928` on base, called from `find` at `:15190`) is an uncoded `Error` reading "find('acct') does not recognise option 'aggregations'…". The REST mapping's unknown-object limb (`packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts:2034`: the quoted object name plus `not`) read that as `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, "Object 'acct' is not registered".
- **What `[]` means on each door.** REST and dispatcher (through `findData`): the 404 above, now 400. `{ groupBy: [] }` alone took the same path to the same 404, so the refusal covers it too. `engine.aggregate` called directly with neither axis returns the rows unchanged (the in-memory aggregator's documented no-axis answer); this PR does not change the engine door (see Acceptance notes).
- **No shipped caller sends `[]` meaning plain rows**, so the ruling's default holds. Measured producers: `objectAggregateSpecQuery` (`@object-ui/core`) always sends one node; `compileListViewGroupQuery` (`@objectstack/spec/ui`) always leads with the `count` node; `ObjectStackAdapter.aggregate` forwards its caller's list; the analytics strategy calls `engine.aggregate`, not `findData`.

`protocol.ts` hunk: `@@ -13435,0 +13436,31 @@`, inside `findData`. It does not overlap #25826 (lines 9021–9060) or #25467 cut 12 (23440–24900).

## Tests

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-aggregate-query-shape-door.test.ts` (7 tests): every refusal asserts `code`, `status` and `httpStatus`, the `path` and `param`, and that no driver read happened. Controls: `date` and `datetime` buckets with their real buckets, a `formula` and an undeclared bucket, an alias that frees the field name, two buckets of one field under their own aliases. A REST-parity block runs `findData` and `mapDataError` for the three card shapes and #25819's empty list (wire `400`, never `404`).
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.empty-aggregate-axis.test.ts` (6 tests): four refused shapes (`code`, `status`, `param`, `object`, engine never asked), plus the served controls.
- **Red first.** With `engine.ts` and `protocol.ts` reverted to `main` (tree-only, restored from saved copies, the diff back to 39 lines before the commit): objectql suite 7 of 7 failed (the control's failure was a read count in the test, corrected); metadata-protocol suite 4 failed, 2 controls passed. With the fix: 7/7 and 6/6.

All at `46a0a7dff1`:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` then `typecheck`: lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`, Test Files 264 passed | 3 skipped, Tests 21496 passed | 19 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test` then `typecheck`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`, Test Files 468 passed, Tests 8725 passed.
- Consumer spot-check (not owed; the engine refuses shapes it used to serve): the 31 `@objectstack/rest` test files that name `aggregations` or `dateGranularity` (31 passed, 516 tests) and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-analytics test` (185 files passed, 4517 tests).
- `eslint --no-inline-config packages/objectql packages/metadata-protocol`: exit 0.
- Derived gates: `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 73 families; all 73 ran with exit 0, reconciled by `--ran` (73 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED). Two needed their prerequisite first, then re-ran green: `check-engine-split-ratio --days 90` (exit 2 on the shallow clone; after `git fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-21`) and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3 before a full `turbo run build`, 121 of 121 tasks).
- Dogfood: n/a (no `!` in the title, no narrowing arm).

## Acceptance notes

- **Uncoded engine option refusal reads as an unknown object.** `rejectUnknownEngineOptions` throws a bare `Error` whose words quote the object name, so any such refusal that reaches a REST data door is mapped to `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` by the quoted-name limb. After this PR no measured REST path reaches it (the empty-list path was the one measured). Observation only, no carrier.
- **The engine door's no-axis answer.** `engine.aggregate(object, {})` and `{ aggregations: [] }` return the raw rows (`ObjectRepository.aggregate` defaults its query to `{}`). The REST door now refuses the same body. No shipped in-process caller was measured sending it. Observation only, no carrier.
- **A `formula` under a date bucket is not judged**, because the declaration names no stored value class for it. On base, a number-expression formula bucketed by month answered one `null` bucket. Observation only, no carrier.
